name: Aschau im Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: Cozy village in the upper Zillertal with the Erlebnisbad Aschau experience pool and authentic Gastronomie.
beschreibung:
Overview

Aschau im Zillertal is a charming municipality in the Schwaz district, situated at an altitude of approximately 567 meters in the heart of the Zillertal. With around 1,900 residents, the village stretches across both banks of the Ziller river, framed by the gentle grassy peaks of the Kitzbühel Alps to the east and the Tux Alps to the west. The highest point in the municipal territory is the 2,442-meter Wimbachkopf. Thanks to its central location on the valley floor, Aschau harmoniously combines genuine Tyrolean village character with prime access to outdoor activities across the entire valley.

History

The settlement was first documented in 1309 under the name Aschove in an episcopal record. Derived from Old High German, the name refers to an ash-tree floodplain forest along the Ziller, symbolized today by a wild duck and reeds in the municipal coat of arms. Early Bavarian farmsteads emerged as early as the 10th century. Over the centuries, the community frequently faced flood hazards from the Achenbach torrent, especially during the disastrous mudslide of 1887, which prompted extensive river control works. During the Tyrolean uprising of 1809, fierce clashes took place at nearby Klausnereck between local Tyrolean sharpshooters and Bavarian-French troops, commemorated today by a stone monument. The Late Neoclassical parish church Maria vom Siege was erected between 1848 and 1849; in 1973, the mountain hamlet of Distelberg formally joined the municipality.

How to Get There

Motorists can easily reach Aschau via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Wiesing/Zillertal and continuing along the Zillertal federal highway B169 for about 15 minutes. Rail passengers travel on ÖBB or DB long-distance trains to Jenbach railway station, where they change seamlessly to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn, which serves Aschau im Zillertal station at regular 30-minute intervals. Regional bus routes connect the village across the valley, and dedicated ski shuttles operate during the winter months.

Tips

In summer, Aschau provides direct access to the scenic Zillertal cycle path and the famous Zillertaler Höhenstraße panoramic road, offering breathtaking alpine vistas across glaciated three-thousanders. The Aufenfeld leisure resort offers a natural swimming lake and the indoor climbing center Kraftreich Aufenfeld. In winter, skiers appreciate the dedicated valley descent from the Hochzillertal-Hochfügen ski resort leading right to the edge of Aschau, while the Zillertal Arena in Zell am Ziller is reachable within minutes. Cross-country skiing trails across the broad valley floor round out the seasonal offerings.
